new_statements.rule_in_words: The only description gives no position for word stress: BPF prosody is said to follow the speakers' L1 Kirundi (a Bantu tone and vowel-length language), with lengthening of some vowels and Kirundi-like tones; French final stress is not asserted. The entire prosody subsection is these two sentences.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is a tendency ('tend to') attributed to Kirundi transfer. In sec. 3.1.1 the author notes Kirundi vowels 'are sometimes lengthened, especially when stressed'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word vs phrase not distinguished ('stress and intonation' treated together); based on the author's recorded corpus of BPF speech.
new_statements.identity_note: Niedzielski's 'Burundi Pidgin French (BPF)' is the L2 pidginized French of Kirundi speakers in Burundi, which he explicitly distinguishes from 'Burundi Broken French' (per the JPCL review snippet); Glottolog buru1323 is based solely on this chapter, so identity is exact. The prosodic statement defers to Kirundi (Glottolog rund1242), a tone/vowel-length language.
